sub_unit_name: Preparation, Properties and engineering applications of PVC and Bakelite, Teflon, Fiber reinforced plastics (FRP)

content.title: Engineering Plastics
content.description: PVC, Bakelite, Teflon, and Fiber Reinforced Plastics (FRP) are important engineering materials widely used because of their excellent mechanical strength, chemical resistance, electrical insulation, and durability.

content.content: Engineering plastics are replacing conventional materials like metals and wood in many industries. Each plastic possesses unique properties that make it suitable for specific engineering applications such as electrical insulation, piping, aerospace, automobiles, and construction.

content.title: Importance
content.content: PVC, Bakelite, Teflon, and FRP are among the most frequently used polymeric materials in engineering due to their versatility and cost-effectiveness.

PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) is prepared by the addition polymerization of vinyl chloride monomer. It is a thermoplastic material known for its excellent chemical resistance, durability, and electrical insulating properties.

rows: Lightweight, corrosion resistant, good electrical insulator
Pipes, cable insulation, water tanks, window frames, medical tubing

content.content: Bakelite is a thermosetting plastic prepared by the condensation polymerization of phenol and formaldehyde. It possesses high mechanical strength, heat resistance, and excellent electrical insulation.

rows: Hard, rigid, heat resistant, electrical insulator
Electrical switches, plug boards, handles, radio and TV casings

content.content: Teflon (Polytetrafluoroethylene) is produced by the addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethylene. It has outstanding chemical resistance, a very low coefficient of friction, excellent thermal stability, and non-stick characteristics.

rows: Non-stick, chemically inert, heat resistant, low friction
Non-stick cookware, chemical containers, bearings, seals, wire insulation

content.content: Fiber Reinforced Plastics (FRP) are composite materials made by reinforcing a polymer matrix with fibers such as glass, carbon, or aramid. The fibers improve the strength, stiffness, and durability of the plastic.

content.title: Common Reinforcing Fibers
content.content: Glass fiber, carbon fiber, and aramid fiber are commonly used to manufacture high-strength FRP composites.

items.question: Corrosion Resistance
items.answer: Resists moisture, chemicals, and atmospheric corrosion.

items.question: Long Service Life
items.answer: Requires minimal maintenance and offers excellent durability.

content.content: PVC is extensively used in plumbing and electrical industries. Bakelite is preferred for electrical insulation and heat-resistant products. Teflon is widely used for non-stick coatings and chemical equipment. FRP finds applications in aerospace, automobiles, marine structures, construction, wind turbine blades, and sports equipment.

right_points: Used in electrical and structural applications

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Remember the preparation method, important properties, and at least three engineering applications of each material, as these are frequently asked in examinations.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: PVC is prepared by addition polymerization of vinyl chloride.
Bakelite is produced by condensation of phenol and formaldehyde.
FRP consists of reinforcing fibers embedded in a polymer matrix.
PVC is used for pipes and insulation.
Bakelite is used in electrical components.
Teflon is famous for its non-stick property.
FRP is widely used in aerospace, automobile, and construction industries.
